entities.summary:
Boniface of Brussels was a Catholic prelate who served as the Bishop of Lausanne from circa 1231 until 1239, when he resigned after agents of Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II assaulted him. This event had significant regional implications, as it highlighted the tensions between the Catholic Church and the Holy Roman Empire. The legacy of Boniface of Brussels can be seen in the continued struggle for ecclesiastical autonomy in Switzerland and the surrounding regions. His relics are housed at the Kapellekerk, and at La Cambre where he died.

Boniface of Brussels was a key figure in the politics of the Holy Roman Empire during the 13th century. His actions and decisions had far-reaching consequences, shaping the course of Swiss history and the relationship between the Catholic Church and the imperial state.
